races.name: Watch Unbridled On attheraces.com Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Kom Tu Voudras
runners_data.note: Faye Bramley's six-year-old is a natural hold-up performer with solid recent form on good ground including a win at the trip, and Harry Cobden in the plate is a significant positive; the race needs enough pace from Motazzen to make the closer's finish count.|
runners_data.comment: Kom Tu Voudras bounced back to winning ways four starts back and has run over today's trip, with a quick eight-day turnaround suggesting she's fit and ready; the fall last time is the one concern connections must put behind them.

runners_data.name: Motazzen
runners_data.note: Henrietta Knight's eight-year-old is the only confirmed pace-maker and that tactical asset is significant, though their overall profile — notably poor figures at the trip and on similar ground — means the position advantage is doing heavy lifting here; watch for whether the pace they set is genuinely honest or deceptively slow.|
runners_data.comment: Motazzen won three starts back and returns here in good order on just 12 days' rest, having run over today's trip before and carrying 159 lb off a mark of 105. The worry is that his two most recent efforts have both disappointed.

runners_data.name: Break Point
runners_data.note: Freddie Keighley claims 5lb for Luke Dace's gelding, who is a hold-up type with a decent record on good ground (1W4P in similar conditions) but whose best runs have come at shorter trips than today's 2m5½f; 37 days off the track without a prep run is a mild query.|
runners_data.comment: Break Point shaped with promise when third two starts back and has the profile of a horse ready to strike after 37 days off, his rating of 108 giving him sound claims at the weights; the worry is he was unplaced three starts back, hinting at inconsistency.

runners_data.name: Easter Icon
runners_data.note: The form line showing a recent win on good ground over 19f gives Gary Brown's mare a live profile here, and Isabelle Ryder (5) fills the prominent role competently; the step up from 19f to 21f is manageable but worth watching given the small field and controlled pace scenario.|
runners_data.comment: Easter Icon has winning form in his last five starts but a brought-down and three poor efforts weigh against him, and he ranks last on our figures here; the 157 lb burden does him no favours either, though he does have experience over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Baltray
runners_data.note: Ben Jones takes the ride on Emma Lavelle's veteran, who is by nature a genuine hold-up horse — the pace map places them in midfield simply because the rear of the field is already occupied by other hold-up types; recent form figures on good ground are modest and the STYLE_FIT flag tempers enthusiasm.|
runners_data.comment: Third three starts back and winless in his last five, Baltray nonetheless heads the ratings on today's trip and returns after a 35-day break with 156 lb to carry — his profile marks him as the one to beat if that placed effort translates here.

races.paceDynamic: Motazzen is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-horse field and, with no genuine rival likely to press them hard for the lead, Brendan Powell can control tempo from the front at a pace of their own choosing over this 2m5½f trip. Easter Icon is a prominent-type who may attempt to sit close, but with Motazzen's natural pace advantage they are unlikely to disrupt the leader's rhythm. The three hold-up horses — Kom Tu Voudras, Break Point, and Baltray (the latter redistributed to midfield on the pace map but a genuine hold-up type by nature) — will be dependent on Motazzen setting enough of a gallop to bring them into the race in the straight. A controlled, uncontested lead on good ground over a staying trip favours a well-placed prominent racer or a strong-finishing hold-up horse with the class to pick them off late, provided the pace does not become too dawdling to suit the closers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Motazzen Controls And Stays
scenarios.trigger: If Motazzen dictates an uncontested, honest gallop and maintains their advantage into the final stages.
scenarios.body: Powell settles Motazzen in front with no rival able to press them, converting the lack of pressure into a controlled, energy-conserving display over the staying trip. This shape suits a prominent or well-placed runner who travels within striking distance rather than a deep hold-up horse who needs a strong pace to reel in a dictator.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Motazzen sets a genuinely strong enough gallop that the hold-up horses can close with purpose in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: A generous pace from Motazzen stretches the field and allows the genuine hold-up types to pick their way through on the run-in at Fontwell's tight track. Kom Tu Voudras, the most consistent hold-up performer on similar going, is best positioned to benefit if the pace does the closers a favour.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Easter Icon Stalks And Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Easter Icon sits close to Motazzen throughout and produces a decisive move at the top of the straight.
scenarios.body: Gary Brown's mare, returning on winning form and strong on good ground, uses her prominent style to shadow the leader and challenge where others cannot respond quickly enough. This shape rewards a horse who can maintain position in a small field without being drawn into a duel.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Suits Baltray
scenarios.trigger: If the race breaks up irregularly or early errors scramble the field, giving Baltray — a true hold-up type shifted to midfield on the map — an unexpected prominent pitch.
scenarios.body: Emma Lavelle's horse is genuinely best suited coming from off the pace, so this scenario only materialises if something disrupts the normal race shape and the pace collapses or accelerates sharply. Even then, Baltray's modest recent form figures on good ground make this the least likely winning shape.

watchPoints.text: Motazzen's true galloping speed is unknown early — if Powell opts for a very sedate pace, the three hold-up horses behind may never get the tow they need and the race becomes a tactical procession for the front end.

Kom Tu Voudras was pulled up on their most recent start (F in form) and while the switch back to good ground is positive, Harry Cobden will need a clean round of jumping over this trip to deliver any late challenge.

Baltray's redistribution to midfield is artificial — Ben Jones may find the horse drifts back to their natural position behind the field regardless, which would leave them with more ground to make up than the pace map suggests.

Easter Icon's apprentice rider Isabelle Ryder (5) has limited experience in a tactical small-field hurdle; how she manages position relative to Motazzen in the early stages could shape whether the prominent profile delivers or gets outmanoeuvred.

Fontwell's tight, figure-of-eight track places a premium on clean jumping and good positioning at the final bend — any jumping error from Motazzen could instantly transform this from a pace-controlled race into an open finish.|

races.name: Download The At The Races App Juvenile Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Grey Sands
runners_data.note: Kim Bailey runner with headgear (visor) and a Flat base showing placed form on standard ground, but this horse's natural role is at the back of the field — the race shape pushes it forward into midfield where it will not be racing comfortably, and zero wins or places over hurdles this term dampens confidence.

runners_data.name: Houndswood Willow
runners_data.note: Tom Dascombe's juvenile has run on good ground before and wears a hood, but has struggled to land a blow over hurdles in six attempts; though a genuine hold-up type by inclination, the shallow pace here means it is being forced to race in a more prominent midfield slot than suits.

runners_data.name: Just Call Me Mo
runners_data.note: A fader in the closing stages by evidence, which is a red flag when the pace is likely to be slow and the run-in at Fontwell is short; the amateur rider Mr Sam Burton takes a 7lb claim but the horse's redistribution into midfield, away from its natural hold-up position, compounds an already unflattering profile.

runners_data.name: Nicolai
runners_data.note: Bradley Harris (3lb claim) partners this Neil Mulholland juvenile who pulled up last time over hurdles — the finishing fade flag and a single piece of relevant good-ground form across six starts makes this a difficult proposition; holding-up naturally but forced forward by the race shape, and the claim matters little if the form is this weak.

runners_data.name: October Surprise
runners_data.note: Sheena West's charge has consistent placed form at staying distances on standard going and Marc Goldstein takes the ride; with no headgear and a hold-up background, this horse should find a natural rhythm just off Rum Diamond and is one of the more likely to genuinely secure a forward position ahead of the redistribution cluster.

runners_data.name: Rum Diamond
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner, Rum Diamond sets the entire pace map here — 151 days off is a significant concern, the fading flag suggests the gallop may become vulnerable late, and the trainer's 14-day record of 0/5 offers no confidence, but its positional advantage is unique in this field.

runners_data.name: Salkadan
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton aboard for the powerful Dan Skelton yard, which has a productive 7/26 14-day strike rate — Salkadan has winning hurdles form and placed form on good going over an appropriate trip, making this the standout profile; hood fitted, and Skelton's intelligence in finding a prominent slot rather than sitting in the hold-up cluster could be decisive.

runners_data.name: Short Symphony
runners_data.note: Laura Horsfall's debutant under Bryan Carver carries the lightest weight (149lbs) and is completely unexposed over hurdles; going suitability, jumping ability, and temperament are all unknown quantities, making any projection speculative, though raw potential over an unfamiliar course cannot be entirely dismissed.

races.paceDynamic: Rum Diamond is the sole confirmed pace-setter and, with no rival likely to dispute the lead aggressively, should dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front on good ground at Fontwell. The eight-runner field is overwhelmingly populated by hold-up types, meaning the race is set up for a single-pace lead with a largely bunched midfield pack tracking at a respectful distance. This field holds more hold-up types than can genuinely settle at the rear: Grey Sands, Houndswood Willow, Just Call Me Mo, and Nicolai are all true hold-up horses mapped to midfield by the race shape, with October Surprise and Salkadan the most likely to actually secure prominent positions behind Rum Diamond. The race shape strongly favours a horse that can travel prominently behind the leader and quicken off a steady pace, making early-position types with genuine finishing gears the primary beneficiaries, while pure hold-up horses face the double jeopardy of racing out of their natural role and needing a strong late injection of pace that a gentle gallop may not generate.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rum Diamond Controls, Stalker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Rum Diamond sets an uncontested, measured gallop and a well-placed tracker picks off the leader approaching the last.
scenarios.body: Rum Diamond bowls along in front at a comfortable tempo, compressing the field and neutralising pure hold-up horses who need a strongly-run race to pounce; any horse that travels fluently just off the pace can glide past at the second-last without burning energy.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Salkadan Dictates From Front
scenarios.trigger: If Salkadan's rider Harry Skelton elects to push forward rather than sit in midfield, turning this into a genuine front-two scenario.
scenarios.body: Skelton's aggressive judgement of pace could see Salkadan bypass the hold-up cluster entirely and race prominently, using his winning hurdles form over course-compatible trips to grind opponents down; Rum Diamond is pressured but neither breaks so the resulting honest gallop still rewards the best traveller.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swamp The Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses late or Rum Diamond fades sharply at the last, opening a gap for horses furthest back to sweep through.
scenarios.body: Redistributed hold-up horses Grey Sands, Houndswood Willow, or Nicolai would need to overcome both their out-of-role midfield position and a race run too steadily to generate the necessary sustained gallop for a late swoop — a scenario dependent on pace collapse rather than tactical design.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Jumping Scrambles Race
scenarios.trigger: If Fontwell's tight track produces jumping errors that reshuffle the field and eliminate the pace-setting advantage Rum Diamond holds.
scenarios.body: A scrambled race benefits the handiest, most versatile horse left standing — Salkadan's proven track record over hurdles at this trip gives resilience, while Short Symphony's unknown jumping profile adds unpredictability to any chaotic scenario.

watchPoints.text: Salkadan — watch whether Harry Skelton slots prominently behind Rum Diamond at the first flight rather than settling in the hold-up pack; if he secures second position this horse's form profile makes it the primary danger throughout.

Rum Diamond — after 151 days off and with a finishing fade pattern, monitor jumping accuracy and whether the lead is maintained approaching the final bend; a sudden weakness here reshapes the entire race.

October Surprise — Marc Goldstein will need to claim one of a limited number of forward positions early; if he is hemmed in behind the redistributed hold-up cluster the horse loses its primary tactical advantage.

Short Symphony — a complete unknown on jumping and temperament at Fontwell; if it jumps fluently in the early stages it could feature, but any jumping hesitation from this debutant may cause interference for horses immediately behind.

Grey Sands and Houndswood Willow — both natural hold-up types forced into midfield by the race shape; watch whether either horse takes a strong hold early, which would signal the jockeys are fighting the pace map and wasting energy before the business end.

races.name: Fontwell Park Family Festival Raceday Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Kotari
runners_data.note: Trained by Gary & Josh Moore and carrying 166lbs on a return from 84 days off, this seven-year-old's recent form (53/34-) shows consistency without a win; a natural hold-up horse pushed to the front by redistribution, which asks a significant question of his tactical adaptability at this track.
runners_data.comment: Consistent without being a winner, Kotari has finished third twice in recent starts and shaped with promise each time, making him a solid each-way threat, though the 84-day absence and a hefty 166 lb in the saddle are the risks to overcome.

runners_data.name: Uncle Remus
runners_data.note: Back just six days after his last run and showing a form string (03-98P) that screams unreliability, Henrietta Knight's five-year-old has placed on soft and good ground but has not won since; operates from hold-up and will need a truly-run race to land a blow.
runners_data.comment: Third four starts back, Uncle Remus shaped better than his recent pulled-up effort suggests, and our rating of 95 marks him as the one to beat in this field; winless in his last five starts, he must bounce back quickly on just six days' rest.

runners_data.name: Delgany Second Now
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's four-year-old won last time out over 22f on good ground and Harry Skelton's booking is significant; his true running style is from hold-up, but the redistribution to midfield may not be far off his natural comfort zone over this longer trip, and his recent winning form is the freshest in the field.
runners_data.comment: Delgany Second Now arrives on the back of a win last time out, his trainer firing at 27% over the past fortnight, and that combination of form and yard confidence makes him a genuine threat here; the concern is a quick three-day turnaround carrying 159 lb.

runners_data.name: Khalk'eau Spigao
runners_data.note: Chris Gordon's four-year-old arrives on 58 days' rest with a consistent placed record absent a win (475-57); a genuine hold-up type wearing a hood, mapped to midfield through redistribution, so his chances hinge on the field spreading out enough for him to deliver a late run.

runners_data.name: Onehundredneighty
runners_data.note: Ben Pauling's six-year-old returns from 100 days off and has placed twice on soft ground, with a best recent finish of second; a natural hold-up horse in a field where his rearward instincts will be compressed, though his stamina profile suits this 2m3f distance.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after 100 days off, Onehundredneighty faces a stiff task here, ranked fifth of seven on our figures; third three starts back offers a crumb of encouragement, but the weight of 153 lb does him no favours.

runners_data.name: North Account
runners_data.note: Flags a patterned tendency to fade in the finish, and five consecutive top-six misses on good ground confirm that concern; Nick Scholfield's six-year-old is a hold-up type mapped to midfield whose fading profile is a significant negative regardless of race shape.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and yet to win in recent starts, North Account returns after 49 days carrying 150 lb, and with several runs still to come before his true level is known, there remains scope for improvement as he steps out again.

runners_data.name: Wise Counsellor
runners_data.note: Gary & Josh Moore's four-year-old (hood, 66 days off) has never won and has a best finish of sixth from eight recorded starts on good ground; a true hold-up runner redistributed to midfield, and the lack of a win alongside weak form figures makes it hard to see a path to the frame.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and yet to win in recent starts, Wise Counsellor returns after 66 days off carrying 149 lb, and with limited form to go on he remains one open to improvement as connections search for a first success.

races.paceDynamic: Kotari is the lone confirmed pace-setter in this field, redistributed to the lead despite being a natural hold-up horse, meaning the pace he sets will be dictated by circumstances rather than instinct — expect a measured, uncontested gallop through the early stages of this 2m3f trip at Fontwell. With no genuine front-runner to press him, Kotari is likely to bowl along at a sustainable rhythm that neither burns off the field early nor creates a scorching finish-line sprint. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Khalk'eau Spigao, Delgany Second Now, Wise Counsellor, Onehundredneighty and North Account all want to race from behind but will be forced into unnatural prominent or midfield positions, meaning the race shape could be surprisingly compressed and tactical. A steady, uncontested gallop with a tightly-bunched pack suits the horse who stays best and whose jockey can position most cleverly from midfield — Delgany Second Now's Harry Skelton angle and recent form on good ground make the Skelton runner the type to capitalise, while any horse that can travel fluently and produce a clean jumping round will be favoured over pure hold-up closers who need pace to run into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kotari Leads, Steadies Field
scenarios.trigger: If Kotari bowls along uncontested and the field tracks him in a compressed bunch at a fair but not punishing gallop.
scenarios.body: Kotari sets an uncontested, controlled tempo and the field strings out naturally from midfield; the race is run at a pace that rewards the best jumper and stayer over the final two flights.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Pick Off Tired Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Kotari's unnatural pace-setting role sees him over-race or tire entering the final mile, gifting hold-up horses a late target.
scenarios.body: Kotari's redistribution to the lead proves costly as he fades from the home turn, and the horses who manage to travel without over-committing can pounce in the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Compressed Midfield Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the artificial pace compression means several horses clash for position early and the race fractures at halfway.
scenarios.body: With so many natural hold-up horses forced into mid-pack positions, jostling for space on Fontwell's tight, figure-of-eight circuit creates a messy race where clean jumping becomes the decisive factor.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Sole Front-Runner Outgallops All
scenarios.trigger: If Kotari settles beautifully in his redistributed role and is never challenged, effectively stealing the race from the front.
scenarios.body: The uncontested lead proves a gift and no horse in the chasing pack is able to bridge the gap up the straight; the race is over before the final flight.

watchPoints.text: Delgany Second Now's last-time-out win over 22f on good ground and the Harry Skelton booking make him the most dangerous runner if the compressed field produces a fair-gallop scenario — watch for Skelton to position him perfectly from midfield.

Kotari's redistribution to the lead is the pivotal race-shape variable — if he over-races or jumps poorly from the front on his first attempt at pace-setting, the whole dynamic collapses and the race becomes a lottery at the last.

The cluster of hold-up horses forced into midfield positions (Khalk'eau Spigao, Onehundredneighty, Wise Counsellor) creates a real risk of traffic and positional interference on Fontwell's tight turns — watch the first few fences for scrimmaging.

Uncle Remus runs just six days after his last start, which combined with an erratic recent form string (03-98P) means Brendan Powell will need a perfectly-judged race — any scrappy early stages could rule him out of contention before halfway.

North Account's flagged tendency to fade in the finish is a concrete negative in a race where hold-up horses are already compromised by redistribution — monitor whether Harry Reed attempts to settle him more prominently than usual to counteract the fading pattern.

races.name: Back A Winner - Birchwood Kia Chichester Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Youdecide
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 21f on good ground, Ben Pauling in excellent 14-day form (3/7), ran just three days ago which is an extremely short turnaround — monitor for freshness concerns, but the recent win and good-ground profile make this a prime candidate in the dominant closing scenario.
runners_data.comment: Youdecide returns just three days after scoring last time out, and that recent winning form is the key angle here; he has run over today's trip and carries 175 lb, though the quick turnaround is worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Edgewell
runners_data.note: Four wins from 15 starts on good ground and a strong recent record (two wins and a third in last four completed), Harry Reed takes over and the tongue tie fits a horse that clearly handles this surface; at OR 94 he holds class in hand over most rivals.
runners_data.comment: Edgewell won back-to-back two and three starts back, returns in sharp order just 13 days since his last outing, and has run over today's trip before, making him a serious threat at the weights; the main concern is his sixth last time out.

runners_data.name: Pawpaw
runners_data.note: Absent for 551 days — the elephant in the room — but his last completed win came on good ground over a similar trip and he holds a tongue tie; trainer Jeffreys has only two 14-day runners suggesting a quiet yard, so fitness after such a lengthy layoff is the critical unknown, and his true style is a hold-up horse now mapped into midfield alongside several similar types.
runners_data.comment: Pawpaw won last time out and has run over today's trip, giving him solid claims here, and his 162 lb burden is a significant impost after a lengthy 551-day absence that must be overcome.

runners_data.name: King Of The Story
runners_data.note: A decade-old gelding who has run 15 times on good ground across his career with three wins and four places, tongue tie fitted; naturally settles at the rear but with the midfield map inflated by fellow hold-up types, he may find himself further forward than ideal — the OR 79 leaves him outclassed at the head of the market.
runners_data.comment: King Of The Story has experience over today's trip but has pulled up twice in his last three starts, and is winless in recent starts; a second four starts back offers some hope, though the burden of 153 lb makes life harder still.

runners_data.name: Helios Allen
runners_data.note: Returning after a mammoth 726-day absence (over two years) which is a near-disqualifying fitness question mark, form figures of 98965 suggest he was deteriorating before his break; a genuine hold-up horse whose best hope is that two years off has freshened him, but the class profile and absence duration make this very hard to trust.
runners_data.comment: Helios Allen rates narrowly clear of these rivals on our figures, and he has run over today's trip before, giving him a solid grounding for the task; the glaring concern, though, is that he is winless in recent starts and returns after a 726-day absence carrying 148 lb.

runners_data.name: Of Corse I Can
runners_data.note: Consistent finisher with five placings in the last six but no win in that sequence, Bradley Harris claims 3lb which partially compensates for OR 71; a natural hold-up horse, good-ground record is modest (1W, 1P from 7) and Neil Mulholland's yard is having a quiet 14-day spell — likely to fill a minor role.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a string of fifth and sixth-place finishes offering little encouragement, Of Corse I Can ranks last on our figures and faces a stiff task under 145 lb, though he has run over today's trip and returns on a reasonable 35-day break.

runners_data.name: Ballinoulart
runners_data.note: The race's sole pace-setter, Richard Upton takes 7lb claim, OR 69 is the lowest in the field and he has zero wins from 11 good-ground runs; his value is entirely positional — he controls the tempo unchallenged — but the class deficit means he is most likely to be swept aside by superior rivals in the closing stages.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked sixth of seven on our figures, Ballinoulart makes this a tough pitch — though he has run over today's trip before and a second two starts back shows he retains some ability, even if a win continues to elude him.

races.paceDynamic: Ballinoulart is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner field and, rated just OR 69, will set a sustainable rather than scorching gallop over the 2m5½f trip on good ground at Fontwell — a course that already rewards jumping fluency and positional awareness over raw pace. With no genuine challenger looking to press him early, Ballinoulart can dictate uncontested from flag to finish, controlling tempo and conserving energy into the final climb. The field behind him is packed with hold-up horses — Youdecide, Edgewell, Pawpaw, King Of The Story, Helios Allen and Of Corse I Can all carry hold-up profiles, meaning the race will string out behind a single pacesetter with closers forced to deliver their challenge on their own terms from the home turn. This shape strongly favours hold-up horses with the class, fitness and finishing kick to reel in a front-runner who has had it all his own way — specifically those towards the top of the handicap like Youdecide and Edgewell who have the form and recent activity to produce a sustained late run. The field holds more genuine hold-up types than can be naturally separated at the rear, with Pawpaw, King Of The Story, Helios Allen and Of Corse I Can all redistributed into the midfield map position — of these, Pawpaw (returning after 551 days) and King Of The Story are the most likely to push into closer positions physically, but none are true pressers of the leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ballinoulart Dictates, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Ballinoulart bowls along at a steady clip and the classier hold-up horses find their stride approaching the last.
scenarios.body: Ballinoulart sets an uncontested pace that flatters the field's hold-up horses, who track through midfield before unleashing their runs from the home turn; the good ground suits a clean-finishing type with class to spare at this level.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If the steady tempo is slow enough that Ballinoulart simply never gets caught, conserving so much energy he finds extra late.
scenarios.body: A falsely slow early gallop means the hold-up horses face too much to do on the flat Fontwell straight, and Ballinoulart, jumping boldly under Upton's positive ride, holds on grimly; his rivals arrive too late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pawpaw Exploits Fresh Comeback
scenarios.trigger: If Pawpaw's 551-day absence has been perfectly timed and he travels strongly enough to produce a race-fit finishing effort.
scenarios.body: Returning from nearly a year and a half off, Pawpaw has the form credentials (won on good ground, OR 88) to belie his layoff if trainer Jeffreys has him spot-on; he travels into the race from midfield and picks up strongly if the pace is honest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Scrappy Finish, Low-Rated Type
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or mid-race scrimmaging disrupts the hold-up brigade and a lower-rated stayer grinds it out.
scenarios.body: Fences cause traffic issues behind Ballinoulart, the classier closers are interfered with or make mistakes, and a dour stayer from the chasing pack — King Of The Story or Of Corse I Can — grinds through to collect.

watchPoints.text: Youdecide ran just three days ago — connections clearly believe he is in the form of his life, but watch for any signs of fatigue or sluggishness at the start that could undermine his hold-up challenge.
Pawpaw's 551-day absence means his physical and jumping sharpness is completely unknown; a rusty jump at an early fence could end his race prematurely and skew the entire finishing order.

Helios Allen returns after 726 days away — if he travels conspicuously well in the early stages, take note as it may signal a long-planned, well-prepared return, but his deteriorating pre-break form makes this a longer-shot alert.

Ballinoulart's early jumping is the key tempo-setter; if he makes a fence error in the first mile and slows to a crawl, the genuine closers will face a falsely slowly-run race that tests their ability to quicken rather than stay.

With five genuine hold-up horses crammed into midfield behind one front-runner, watch for early jostling and positioning between Edgewell, Youdecide and Pawpaw — whoever secures the best tracking position two from home is likely to have first run at the leader.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Mares' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Camshaft
runners_data.note: Sole front runner with recent wins at Fontwell and 2 from 6 in similar good going — Jonjo O'Neill Jr. rides, the five-year-old is improving rapidly and the uncontested lead at a turning track is a significant tactical gift; cheekpieces worn.
runners_data.comment: Camshaft arrives on the back of back-to-back wins two and three starts ago, and though third last time out, she remains in cracking nick; carrying a hefty 168 lb after 44 days off is the one concern.

runners_data.name: Mobile Mamma
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton in the plate is an immediate upgrade, and her five-run record at Fontwell includes a course win over this trip in good ground — tongue strap fitted, she is a genuine hold-up type who needs a true pace and will need things to set up perfectly from off them.
runners_data.comment: Mobile Mamma has been knocking on the door, finishing third and then second in her last two starts before an unplaced effort, and 21 days gives her a clean freshening; the concern is that 161 lb is a hefty weight to carry while still seeking that elusive first win.

runners_data.name: Luna Run
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with two wins at this 26f trip in good ground and the best course-and-distance profile of the closers; Harry Derham's yard is quiet in the last fortnight but the form credentials make her the most natural challenger to Camshaft's dominance from a tracking position.
runners_data.comment: Luna Run showed a winner one start back but has been in and out of form otherwise, and ranked sixth of seven on our figures she faces a stiff task under 156 lb, though she does have experience over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Steal A Glance
runners_data.note: Steps up sharply in trip — all five starts have been over 17-18f — which raises a major stamina question, even if she has the prominent profile to be competitive in the early exchanges; the amateur apprentice Chad Bament takes 5lb and ran just three days ago.
runners_data.comment: Steal A Glance arrives here just three days after finishing second last time out, and that near-miss is the standout angle for a filly who commands the highest rating in this field; winless in her last five starts, she will need to convert promise into reward under 151 lb.

runners_data.name: Athena's Dream
runners_data.note: Young four-year-old with decent placed form including a second over 24f in good ground, racing prominently, but the 7lb claimer Megan Bevan is the least experienced pilot in the field; no headgear, trainer has had no runners in the last 14 days.

runners_data.name: Lynsey Larue
runners_data.note: Ran just yesterday which demands a significant stamina flag — she has winning form over 24f in similar conditions and hold-up pedigree over this trip, but the back-to-back-day schedule is highly unusual and warrants close scrutiny before assessing her chance at a fair price.
runners_data.comment: Ran just yesterday and already back out carrying 150 lb, which makes her hard to fancy; she was pulled up two starts back, though a winner three starts back and third last time out are the positives in an otherwise testing profile.

runners_data.name: Glorious Mist
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old whose recent form reads PP-F with 96 days off; a genuine rear-of-field type who finds her natural position squeezed out in this small field, reducing the effectiveness of her hold-up style — her low OR of 67 and patchy jumping record compound the concerns.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts yet her rating of 92 puts her firmly in contention here, and experience over today's trip is a clear asset at 142 lb; the main concern is a troubled recent spell of falls and pull-ups that makes her current wellbeing hard to gauge after 96 days off.

races.paceDynamic: Camshaft is the lone confirmed front runner and, with no genuine rival to dispute the lead, she will dictate terms at whatever tempo suits Jonjo O'Neill Jr. over this 3m2f trip at Fontwell. Luna Run and Steal A Glance are the likely prominent pair who will track behind, but neither has the profile to seriously challenge for the front, meaning Camshaft controls pace shape from flag to finish. Mobile Mamma, Lynsey Larue, and Glorious Mist are the hold-up contingent, though the field holds more prominent/hold-up types than can all find their natural position — Glorious Mist, a genuine rear-of-field horse, has been mapped to midfield because the true back of the field is already crowded, and she is unlikely to secure deep cover in a seven-runner race at this trip. An uncontested, unexposed five-year-old dictating from the front over a staying trip on a tight, turning course is a significant tactical advantage, and this race shape strongly favours a prominent-to-front profile that can control fractions and resist late pressure — the hold-up runners face the most ground to make up with limited room for Camshaft to be reeled in.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Camshaft Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Camshaft settles into an uncontested lead and rolls at a pace that drains the stamina of hold-up types.
scenarios.body: Camshaft dictates every yard, the moderate pace at Fontwell's turning track suits a horse who can quicken when asked, and the field arrives at the last with insufficient momentum to overhaul her. Luna Run or Steal A Glance, tracking close throughout, are best placed to inherit if Camshaft tires but the front runner's profile is dominant here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhauling Tiring Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Camshaft goes too fast early and ties up in the final half-mile, allowing a prominent tracker to sweep by.
scenarios.body: Luna Run has solid course and distance form in similar going and could pick up sharply if Camshaft over-extends herself trying to build an unassailable lead. Steal A Glance is less exposed over this longer trip and could stay on past a fading Camshaft, though her recent form at shorter distances is a concern.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly strong and sustained, draining front and prominent runners before the last, allowing a closer to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: Mobile Mamma has winning form at Fontwell over similar trips in good ground and Harry Skelton gives her strong claims if she gets the right setup, but Lynsey Larue also has 3m+ winning form to call on. Glorious Mist's deep hold-up style is compromised by being pushed into midfield in a small field, significantly reducing her effectiveness in this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and Attrition
scenarios.trigger: If there are significant jumping errors or fallers that scramble the race order completely.
scenarios.body: Over a 3m2f handicap hurdle with multiple hold-up mares, a messy jumping incident could elevate an otherwise outpaced runner into contention by fortune. Athena's Dream is young and lightly raced enough to be unphased by a chaotic race, and Lynsey Larue's recent course form keeps her in the picture.

watchPoints.text: Lynsey Larue ran yesterday — monitor if she travels with her usual fluency or ties up from fatigue before the final two hurdles, as a struggling runner in a tight Fontwell field can disrupt those behind her.

Camshaft's jumping must be tracked from the first — she is a five-year-old front runner and if she makes errors early, the tempo will become erratic and benefit hold-up types like Mobile Mamma and Lynsey Larue.
Glorious Mist's jumping record (two Pulled-Ups, a Fall in last three starts) is a serious in-running hazard over 3m2f — any serious blunder or exit could bring down nearby horses in a compact field.

Watch how quickly Steal A Glance capitulates if this trip proves too far — her dropping away from Camshaft's position would be a reliable mid-race indicator that the front runner's lead is safe and the hold-up horses are outpaced.

Luna Run's position after the third hurdle is the key tell — if she tracks Camshaft within two lengths travelling smoothly, she is the most likely alternative winner; if she drifts back to midfield she is likely beaten.

races.name: Free Tips Daily On attheraces.com Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Person of Interest
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse with a strong record in similar good ground (2W, 5P from 13 sim-going runs), but Fontwell's tight circuit is notoriously unkind to horses that need daylight late; Harry Cobden is an excellent navigator but 47 days off the track for a 6-year-old chaser warrants monitoring.
runners_data.comment: Person of Interest showed his class when winning two starts back, and followed up with a second last time out to advertise strong current form; carrying 167 lb after 47 days off is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: She Is For Me Boys
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with a tongue tie and a solid Fontwell course record in similar going (8/11, 4W); Isabelle Ryder's 5lb claim reduces the weight burden, and if she secures a clean lead and jumps fluently she is the one all others have to beat in this shape.
runners_data.comment: She Is For Me Boys arrives as the top-rated runner in this field, her recent form reading consistently competitive with a win two starts back and a placed effort last time out, and she has experience over today's trip; the concern is whether 60 days between runs leaves her spot-on for this test.

runners_data.name: Merely A Detail
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse who showed a smart win over 16f in good ground and is lightly weighted at 164lbs; trainer Toby Bulgin has no recent runners to assess form on, and the V (void) in recent form is worth noting as it suggests interrupted preparation rather than a clear run of fitness.
runners_data.comment: Merely A Detail brings a win two starts back into this, and while the most recent run was voided she returns after 35 days in decent order, has run over today's trip, and her 164 lb burden is the one watch point.

runners_data.name: Two To Tango
runners_data.note: Proven prominent racer with an outstanding sim-going record (13/15, 1W, 11P) and every run in the formbook on good ground at 2m+ making this trip and surface completely familiar; the patience headgear (p) suits the race shape if she can track the leaders and produce a late thrust from a prominent position.
runners_data.comment: Placed second two starts back and third three starts back, Two To Tango has the profile of a genuine danger here, and our rating of 111 underlines his claims; the main concern is a 73-day absence since his last start.

runners_data.name: A Little Something
runners_data.note: Hat-trick winner seeking four consecutive victories and clearly relishes good ground (11/15 sim-going), but the form string includes U and F — jumping errors under pressure are a live concern, especially if she is pressured into a fierce duel with She Is For Me Boys from the outset.
runners_data.comment: A Little Something has winning form three and four starts back, but a fall and an unseating in her two most recent outings make her very hard to trust, and our rating has her well held by the field's top performers at the weights.

runners_data.name: Martin's Denuo
runners_data.note: All three wins have come in heavy or soft conditions, making the jump to good ground a significant unknown; the hood and tongue tie suggest a horse that can be free or difficult to settle, and at just 4 years old in a handicap chase with an apprentice rider, the risk profile is high despite his rapid improvement.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, Martin's Denuo arrives in fine nick with three wins in his last five starts, including back-to-back victories, and 26 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh and ready.

races.paceDynamic: She Is For Me Boys and A Little Something will contest the early lead, creating a genuine front-running duel from the first fence over this 2m2f trip at Fontwell. She Is For Me Boys has strong course form and the headgear of a horse that needs to be in front, while A Little Something arrives on a hat-trick of wins and will not concede the lead without a fight — Ben Jones is unlikely to drop away voluntarily. This contested early pace should produce an honest, even gallop that places a premium on stamina and jumping accuracy in the latter stages, as neither front-runner is likely to coast. This race shape — with pace genuinely on from the front and the field stretched — favours prominent-to-lead types that can control their own destiny, while hold-up horses face the biggest ask given Fontwell's tight, turning nature makes late sprints from off the pace difficult to execute.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runners Battle It Out
scenarios.trigger: If She Is For Me Boys or A Little Something dominates from the front and the duel burns off rivals before the home straight.
scenarios.body: The contested early pace sets a genuine gallop, and whichever of the two front-runners jumps better and settles marginally in front will have the rail to herself heading to the final fences; Fontwell's undulating, turning track rewards those who can control tempo and conserve jumping momentum. Two To Tango, with an excellent sim-going record and prominent style, is ideally placed to pounce if either leader weakens late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the front-running duel burns both leaders out before the last and the closest pursuer swoops.
scenarios.body: Two To Tango has won at 2m4f in similar good-ground conditions and her patient-prominent style means she avoids the attrition of the early battle while staying close enough to pounce; her 13/15 sim-going record underlines how suited she is when this type of gallop unfolds. Person of Interest, despite preferring hold-up tactics, is a dual winner in similar going and would also benefit if the pace produces a strung-out field she can pick through.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Home
scenarios.trigger: If the front-running duel is exceptionally fierce and the field is sufficiently strung out to create a clear gap for a late finisher.
scenarios.body: Person of Interest has won twice and placed five times in similar going, and a truly punishing pace could theoretically leave an opening at Fontwell if runners tire into the final bend; however, the tight turning course makes this scenario genuinely hard to execute for a pure hold-up horse. Merely A Detail, a 5-year-old hold-up type who won over this sort of distance in good ground, represents the secondary option if the race truly falls apart at the front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Improver Lands A Blow
scenarios.trigger: If Martin's Denuo's rapid progression as a young improver (three wins from his last three) translates to this chase environment despite limited comparable form.
scenarios.body: The 4-year-old has shown a sharp upward curve but all his form is on heavy/soft ground, and his unknown-style tag means his tactical position is uncertain on debut over these fences in this company; if he settles into a rhythm and jumps cleanly, raw ability could compensate. The headgear notes (hood and tongue tie) suggest a horse that needs managing, and the 5lb claim of Rian Corcoran is a moderate mitigation.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether A Little Something or She Is For Me Boys blinks first in the opening mile — if one capitulates early, the other inherits a solo lead and the whole race dynamic changes dramatically.

Martin's Denuo's jumping must be monitored from fence one; all his experience is on soft/heavy ground and a stumble or sprawling jump on quicker turf at Fontwell's tight bends could end his race or take out a rival.
Person of Interest is 47 days off the track and holds a hold-up style on a course that compresses finishing speed — if she is not travelling smoothly by the water jump, her chance is likely gone.

Two To Tango's trainer Emma Lavelle also saddles A Little Something, creating a potential stable tactics angle — watch whether Charlie Todd sits closer than expected or allows the front-runners to fight while he conserves energy two lengths off the pace.

Merely A Detail's recent V (void) in the form string means her true fitness level is uncertain; if she shows any signs of rustiness at the first two fences, her hold-up role becomes even harder to execute in a race that is likely to be run at a genuine clip.

races.name: Free Bets On attheraces.com Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: God Of Fire
runners_data.note: Likely to race prominently or on the pace here and is the only confirmed front-runner in the field; Jonjo O'Neill Jr. is adept at making the most of a clear lead on a tight track, and 13 days' freshness is fine — the STYLE_FIT flag means discount if the shape requires a truly dominant front-running performance.
runners_data.comment: Won two starts back and rates a clear nine pounds above his official mark on our assessment; God Of Fire has run over today's trip and returns on a sharp 13-day turnaround carrying 168 lb, with that fourth last time out the only minor concern.

runners_data.name: Best Night
runners_data.note: Consistent placer on good ground with five of his last five runs on similar going, and David Pipe's yard is in form (1/10 T14); tongue-tie noted, and as a true hold-up horse he needs the pace to be genuine to deliver his best finishing effort from the rear.
runners_data.comment: Consistent form figures of second and third in recent starts make Best Night a genuine threat here, and she has run over today's trip; the main risk is that she remains winless in her last five outings.

runners_data.name: Aggagio
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old who has shown useful placed form from a prominent position, with Gary & Josh Moore returning 2/21 in the last 14 days; the blinkers are a key headgear note and his best runs at similar distances on good ground suggest he is well-suited by this trip and surface.
runners_data.comment: Aggagio is winless in his last five starts yet shaped with promise when third last time out, and he has run over today's trip before; carrying 166 lb on a 28-day break is the chief concern for a gelding our rating marks as the second-strongest in the field.

runners_data.name: Brave Guest
runners_data.note: A four-year-old lightly weighted at OR 100 who has posted two consecutive runner-up finishes on good ground; marc Goldstein takes the ride for a small yard (T14: 1/4) and 46 days off the track is worth noting — from a hold-up position he needs the race to truly develop to get competitive.
runners_data.comment: Brave Guest arrives here on the back of consecutive second-place finishes two and three starts back, boasts experience over today's trip, and at 166 lb our rating of 104 suggests he holds strong claims against this field; the concern is he remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Double Power
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse who fades in the finish, with a string of mid-to-rear finishes in handicap hurdles at this trip and beyond; Harry Skelton is the booking but the trainer is 0/4 in the last 14 days and the tp headgear has not converted his prominence into wins — treat with significant caution.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked sixth of nine on ratings, Double Power faces a stiff ask under 165 lb, though he returns on a sharp 15-day turnaround and has enough class on an official mark of 96 to warrant respect if the headwinds ease.

runners_data.name: Graffiti
runners_data.note: A 7lb claimer in Megan Bevan takes the ride for a small yard that is 0/2 T14; Graffiti holds a win on good ground at 10f but steps back up in trip here and as a hold-up horse on a track where position is hard to recover, the apprentice allowance must compensate for the positional disadvantage.
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and second two starts back, Graffiti shows consistent placing form yet remains winless in his last five starts, and 52 days off the track is a fitness query; the 160 lb burden is no help, though he has run over today's trip and our rating of 99 suggests some upside.

runners_data.name: Charlie My Boy
runners_data.note: A veteran nine-year-old whose form figures include a recent second from a hold-up style — his natural place is at the back of the field, not the midfield position shown on the map, so the race shape offers him less assistance than it appears; Jenkins' yard is 1/6 T14 and 59 days off adds a freshness question.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked seventh of nine on our figures, Charlie My Boy has plenty to prove here; he has run over today's trip and the second last time out is a crumb of comfort, but 160 lb is a hefty burden for a horse without a win to his name.

runners_data.name: Raffles Nobu
runners_data.note: Ran just five days ago but has sound recent form including a win and two places at this sort of trip on good ground; Quinlan takes over in the saddle for Scholfield's yard (2/10 T14) and the tb headgear combination suggests a horse who races prominently and keeps finding — well-placed in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Raffles Nobu is hard to fancy ranked bottom but one on our figures, and a fifth last time out — just five days ago — does little to help his cause; he has run over today's trip and does own a win in his last six starts, but 160 lb is a stern burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Harry Gulliver
runners_data.note: Won over 20f on good ground and has placed figures to recommend him, but his genuine hold-up style means he is in reality further back than the midfield slot on the map suggests; Bryan Carver rides for a yard with 1/5 T14, and off 35 days he needs a strongly run race to deliver his kick from a wide position on a turning track.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of nine on our figures, Harry Gulliver has finished fifth and eighth in his last two starts, making him hard to fancy here. A third three starts back offers slim encouragement, as does the win four starts back, but he faces a stiff ask from 149 lb.

races.paceDynamic: God Of Fire is the lone confirmed pace-setter here and should control this race from the front at a measured, sustainable gallop over 2m1½f on good ground at Fontwell. Aggagio, Double Power, and Raffles Nobu will push to race prominently behind him, creating an orderly, single-file pace rather than a contested or pressured lead. The hold-up brigade of Best Night, Brave Guest, and Graffiti will be forced to settle in the rear, with Charlie My Boy and Harry Gulliver — both true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map — actually likely to race further back than shown, meaning they face a stiffer test of finishing kick than the shape implies. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can track the pace throughout and pounce from close order, as the moderate tempo will not generate enough end-to-end gallop to bring late closers off the pace into contention.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If God Of Fire sets a controlled pace and the prominent trio track comfortably before one kicks clear in the home straight.
scenarios.body: God Of Fire, Aggagio, and Raffles Nobu are ideally placed to stalk and strike, with the measured gallop rewarding those who never leave the front group; the winner is most likely to emerge from the first four or five home at the second-last.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If God Of Fire travels exceptionally well, builds a small advantage at the top of the straight, and the challengers leave their run too late.
scenarios.body: God Of Fire has a STYLE_FIT note suggesting he races prominently but is capable of leading, and on this track's tight turns a horse in front can steal a march before rivals can organise a challenge; the good ground suits and Jonjo O'Neill Jr. is a sharp judge of pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected, stringing out the field and burning off the prominent horses before the final hurdle.
scenarios.body: Best Night has solid place form on good ground from a well-placed yard and could emerge as the strongest finisher if the race is run to suit late closers; Brave Guest has shown consistent placed form and could also benefit from a genuinely run race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Disrupts Shape
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent horse over-commits early or there are jumping errors that shuffle the pack and break the rhythm of the leading group.
scenarios.body: Double Power's record of fading finishes makes it a candidate to disappear, and if multiple horses make errors at Fontwell's unusual fences the tactical order could be dismantled entirely; in that scenario the best-jumping survivor from the prominent group or a well-ridden, fresh challenger benefits.

watchPoints.text: God Of Fire is the only horse capable of controlling the pace — if he is taken on early by Aggagio or Raffles Nobu, the entire shape collapses and a hold-up horse could profit unexpectedly.

Double Power is flagged as a horse that fades in the finish and is prominent in style — watch for him to set a false tempo before emptying after the third-last, potentially distorting the race for those behind him.

Charlie My Boy and Harry Gulliver are true hold-up horses shown in midfield on the map; if they drift back to their natural position the rear of the field could become congested, creating traffic problems in the straight at Fontwell's tight circuit.

Best Night holds a headgear note (tongue-tie) and five consecutive runs on good ground with solid placed form — if the pace quickens earlier than expected he is the hold-up horse most likely to close meaningfully from off the pace.

Raffles Nobu runs only five days after his last start; watch the market and his behaviour in the paddock — if he travels well and settles behind God Of Fire he is the prominent horse best-placed to capitalise on this pace setup.
